drafts.spl: index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 Image="*\\powershell.exe" (match(ParentImage, "(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook)\\.exe$")) (match(CommandLine, "(?i)\\s-enc(odedcommand)?\\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{10,}")) | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 match(Image, "(?i)\\\\powershell\.exe$") match(ParentImage, "(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook)\.exe$") match(CommandLine, "(?i)\s-e(nc|ncodedcommand)?\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{10,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 | where match(Image, "(?i)\\\\powershell\.exe$") AND match(ParentImage, "(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook)\.exe$") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)\s-(e|enc|ec|encodedcommand)\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") AND NOT match(CommandLine, "(?i)\s-(file|f)\s+\S+\.ps1") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*WINWORD.EXE" OR ParentImage="*EXCEL.EXE" OR ParentImage="*OUTLOOK.EXE") | where match(ParentImage,"(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook)\\.exe$") AND match(CommandLine,"(?i)\\s-e[a-z]*[:\\s]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*WINWORD.EXE" OR ParentImage="*EXCEL.EXE" OR ParentImage="*OUTLOOK.EXE") | where match(ParentImage,"(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook)\\.exe$") AND match(CommandLine,"(?i)\\s[-/]e[a-z]*[:\\s]+[\"']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

gates.gate_spl: search index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*WINWORD.EXE" OR ParentImage="*EXCEL.EXE" OR ParentImage="*OUTLOOK.EXE") | where match(ParentImage,"(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook)\\.exe$") AND match(CommandLine,"(?i)\\s[-/]e[a-z]*[:\\s]+[\"']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | bin _time span=20m | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by _time Computer, User, ParentImage, Image | sort 0 - count

findings.detail: The switch regex `-(e|enc|ec|encodedcommand)` only enumerates four spellings, but PowerShell accepts any unambiguous prefix of -EncodedCommand. Variants such as -en, -enco, -encod, -encode, -encoded, -encodedc, -encodedco, -encodedcom, -encodedcomm, -encodedcomma, -encodedcomman are all honored by powershell.exe and none of them match, so an attacker performing the exact attack_step (office -> powershell with -EncodedCommand base64) is fully missed by choosing e.g. `-enco`.
findings.fix_hint: Match the switch by prefix instead of fixed list, e.g. (?i)\s-e(n(c(o(d(e(d(c(o(m(m(a(n(d)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?\s+ or a broader `\s-e[a-z]*\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` anchored to the encoded-command family.

findings.detail: The exclusion `AND NOT match(CommandLine, '(?i)\s-(file|f)\s+\S+\.ps1')` is attacker-controllable. The CommandLine only has to CONTAIN a ` -f something.ps1` substring to suppress the alert; an attacker can append a harmless decoy token (e.g. ` -f c:\x.ps1`) after the real `-enc <base64>` payload, or the PowerShell format operator `-f "...ps1"` inside a string, and the whole detection is dropped while the encoded command still executes.
findings.fix_hint: Do not use a negative CommandLine filter to distinguish file vs encoded launches; instead gate positively on presence of the encoded-command switch only, and drop the -file/-f exclusion (an encoded command and -File are mutually exclusive anyway).

findings.detail: The regex requires whitespace after the switch (`\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]`). PowerShell also accepts colon-delimited parameter syntax, e.g. `-enc:<base64>` or `-e:<base64>`, which contains no space before the value and therefore never matches.
findings.fix_hint: Allow a colon or equals separator: `(?i)\s-e[a-z]*[:\s]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}`.

findings.detail: Detection keys only on Image ending in \powershell.exe. Sysmon EventID 1 also carries OriginalFileName, which remains PowerShell.EXE when the binary is copied/renamed (e.g. office macro drops %TEMP%\svc.exe = copy of powershell.exe and spawns it with -enc). Such a renamed-but-still-PowerShell launch from winword/excel/outlook satisfies the attack idea yet Image never matches.
findings.fix_hint: Also test OriginalFileName, e.g. match(OriginalFileName,'(?i)^PowerShell\.EXE$') OR match(Image,...), so renamed copies of powershell.exe are caught.

findings.detail: The base search retrieves every Sysmon EventCode=1 event and applies four regex via `where match()` with no index-time string pre-filter. On a busy fleet this scans all process-creation events every 15 minutes. Adding cheap CommandLine/ParentImage keyword filters in the base search would prune the dataset before regex.
findings.fix_hint: Add `CommandLine="*powershell*" (ParentImage="*winword*" OR ParentImage="*excel*" OR ParentImage="*outlook*")` to the base search before the where/match stage.

findings.detail: ParentImage is limited to winword|excel|outlook, which matches attack_steps. Other common Office payload launchers (powerpnt.exe, mshta, wscript spawned by Office) are a different chain and out of scope here; noting only that the list is narrow relative to real Office-to-PowerShell abuse.
findings.fix_hint: If desired later, extend the Office parent list, but do not widen past the stated attack_steps for this rule.

evasion_events.note: Abbreviated-prefix switch -enco (valid PowerShell prefix of -EncodedCommand) is not in the regex alternation (e|enc|ec|encodedcommand), so this office->powershell encoded launch is missed.

evasion_events.note: Colon-delimited parameter syntax -enc:<base64> has no whitespace before the value, so the \s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,} requirement fails and the event is missed.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS04.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Users\Public\svc.exe</Data><Data Name='OriginalFileName'>PowerShell.EXE</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Users\Public\svc.exe" -enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAIABOAGUAdAA=</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\bwayne</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE"</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Office macro copies powershell.exe to a renamed path and launches it with -enc; OriginalFileName is still PowerShell.EXE but Image no longer ends in powershell.exe, so the Image regex misses it.

findings.detail: The CommandLine regex `(?i)\s-e[a-z]*[:\s]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` requires the character immediately after the switch separator to be a base64 character. PowerShell accepts the encoded blob wrapped in quotes (e.g. `-enc "<base64>"`, also single quotes), which it strips before decoding. When the value is quoted, the char after `[:\s]+` is `"` (not in `[A-Za-z0-9+/=]`), so the match fails and the exact attack_step (office -> powershell -enc base64) is fully missed. This is independent of the four prior findings.
findings.fix_hint: Allow an optional quote between the separator and the base64, e.g. `[:\s]+[\"']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}`, or extract/normalise the -enc argument value before matching.

findings.detail: The switch pattern hardcodes a hyphen (`\s-e[a-z]*`). powershell.exe also honours the forward-slash parameter prefix, so `powershell /enc <base64>` (or `/e`, `/encodedcommand`) executes the same encoded payload but never matches because the regex only looks for `-e`. A realistic variant of the attack_step is fully missed.
findings.fix_hint: Accept either prefix in the regex, e.g. `\s[-/]e[a-z]*[:\s]+...`.

findings.detail: Detection relies solely on ParentImage office filter plus the CommandLine `-e*` regex and places no constraint on Image/OriginalFileName. This correctly catches renamed-powershell children (good, resolving the prior Image-only concern), but it also means any office-parented child whose CommandLine happens to carry a 20+ char token after a `-e...` switch will fire; no benign source is visible in the rows, so impact is low.
findings.fix_hint: Optionally add an OriginalFileName=PowerShell.EXE OR Image ...powershell.exe assertion to reduce incidental matches while keeping rename coverage.

findings.detail: ParentImage is limited to winword|excel|outlook, matching attack_steps. Other Office launchers (powerpnt.exe, mshta/wscript spawned by Office) are a different chain and out of scope; noted only as narrow coverage, no change requested.
findings.fix_hint: No action required within the current attack idea.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -enc "SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAKQA="</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: WINWORD spawns powershell with -enc and the base64 wrapped in double quotes. The quote sits where the regex expects a base64 char ([:\s]+ then [A-Za-z0-9+/=]), so match() fails and the alert is dropped though the encoded command still runs.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" /enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAKQA=</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: WINWORD spawns powershell using the forward-slash prefix /enc instead of -enc. PowerShell honours /enc identically, but the regex only matches `\s-e`, so this is missed.

findings.detail: The CommandLine regex floors the base64 blob at 20 characters (`[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}`). PowerShell encoded commands for short payloads are well under 20 chars: a short bootstrap/stager such as `-enc` of a 4-8 char command encodes to ~12-16 base64 chars. e.g. `calc` in UTF-16LE base64 is `YwBhAGwAYwA=` (12 chars), and a terse download/`iex` one-liner stager can also be crafted short. An office->powershell -enc chain (the exact attack_step) with a short encoded value is fully missed. The floor is purely a noise guard an attacker can stay under.
findings.fix_hint: Lower the minimum token length (e.g. {8,} or {4,}), or key the detection on the presence of the `-e*`/`/e*` encoded switch itself (Image=powershell + switch) rather than on blob length.

findings.detail: The switch regex matches a single prefix char `[-/]e[a-z]*`. PowerShell 7 (pwsh.exe) and some invocations honour the POSIX double-dash form `--encodedcommand <b64>`; `\s--encodedcommand` would see `-` then `-` (not `e`) and fail. attack_steps name powershell.exe specifically and 5.1 does not accept `--`, so this is narrow/edge coverage only; no change requested.
findings.fix_hint: If pwsh.exe is in scope, allow `-{1,2}` before the `e` switch.

findings.detail: Schedule runs every 15 minutes (`*/15`) with a 20-minute lookback window, so each 5-minute overlap re-reads events already alerted on, producing duplicate alerts for the same encoded-command event. hits_per_day is 0.14 so volume impact is negligible, but duplicate notables are possible.
findings.fix_hint: Align window to the cadence (15m window for */15) or dedup on Computer+CommandLine+firstTime.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -enc YwBhAGwAYwA=</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Real WINWORD->powershell -enc chain (exact attack_step) but the encoded blob `YwBhAGwAYwA=` is only 12 base64 chars, below the regex `{20,}` floor, so the search never matches. A short encoded stager/launcher evades purely by length.
